short-term supplementation of aged dogs with acetyl-l- carnitine (ALC) and lipoic (LA) acid did not alter cognitive performance in aged dogs.
supplementation with acetyl-L-carnitine or alpha-lipoic acid alone did not improve cognition in older dogs.
short-term supplementation of acetyl-l-carmite and lipoic acids does not improve cognition or reduce oxidative damage in aged dogs.

the diet enriched in antioxidants and mitochondrial co- factors improved cognition in aged dogs and that this was associated with a reduction in brain oxidative damage.

the beneficial effects on cognition in aged dogs of a diet enriched with mitochondrial co-fac-tors and antioxidants may not be attributable to the mitochondrial co-factors alone.
